refutation_attempt: Looked for anything that pumps or signals Guide results: no library caller of RenderPending*, Update and UpdateAsync empty, GuideAction handle constructed signalled and never Set or Reset. Every other Begin* completes at construction. Compared summary and quotes with the code.
reason: Real. But the summary says UpdateAsync always returns true; it returns isInitialized_, so false before Initialize. The entry also quotes 'has not been answered yet' for both End calls; the keyboard one says 'has not been confirmed yet'. Message-box and keyboard results complete only via the render hook, an injected click or Enter; the wait handle is pre-signalled.

correction.summary: The dispatcher's Update advances nothing and UpdateAsync only reports whether Initialize has run, and the Guide results that stay pending expose an already-signalled wait handle, so a pump loop on a pending Guide result spins forever and WaitOne returns before End can succeed.

refutation_attempt: Traced ReadRequestBody for chunked, length-less and truncated requests: contentLength stays 0 or the body loop breaks when recv returns 0 or an error, yet the function returns true and Listen answers 200. Checked the design comment verbatim and that tests send only complete requests.
reason: The design comment promises that unreadable pushes are refused, but only a failed header read or a header block over 1 MiB yields 400. Length-less and chunked requests get 200 and are dropped, truncated bodies get 200 and are queued, and the declared length is uncapped. Low: only non-CNA or failing senders.

refutation_attempt: Looked for SO_RCVTIMEO, poll, a wake-up descriptor, or Close touching the accepted socket: none. Close shuts down only listenSocket_ then joins the worker, which sits in recv on a different descriptor. Tests: every client sends a full request and closes. Distinct from BUG-164's race.
reason: The single worker reads each accepted connection with a blocking recv and no deadline, and Close only shuts the listening socket before join, so a silent connected peer makes Close and the destructor wait without bound. Loopback-only peers keep exposure narrow, so medium is arguable but not clearly mis-set.

refutation_attempt: Searched for escaping before concatenation and for XML parsing in the channel: neither exists. The header's 'wire form' sentence sits on the raw class, but the toast reuses that Windows Phone wire form; an ampersand or angle bracket in Title or SubTitle yields ill-formed XML.
reason: ToastPushNotificationMessage::SendAsync concatenates Title and SubTitle into the toast XML verbatim, so an ampersand or angle bracket produces ill-formed or restructured XML. The sender has no escaping and the channel does not parse, so the receiving handler gets broken bytes. The contract is implicit in the wire form but sound.

refutation_attempt: Weighed the constructor's 'unique within the application' precondition against Find's 'null when no channel of that name is open'. Traced Open (unconditional map assignment) and Close (identity-checked erase): closing the newer duplicate erases the name while the older still listens.
reason: Real and reachable, but only when a caller breaks the documented uniqueness precondition; the identity-checked erase shows the registry was meant to tolerate replacement, and Find's contract is violated once the newer duplicate closes first. Low severity is right; no test opens two same-named channels.

refutation_attempt: Traced DispatchPendingNotificationsEXT: pending_ is swapped into a local before the raise loop, and Sharp Runtime's EventHandler::Raise iterates a snapshot with no try/catch, so a throwing handler destroys the remaining bodies. Checked nothing re-queues them.
reason: A throwing HttpNotificationReceived handler leaves the loop and the local batch, already acknowledged with 200, is destroyed. 'Every notification that has arrived' binds weakly on an exceptional path, so this is a low exception-safety bug; Raise's no-catch behaviour is read from an unpinned sibling checkout.

refutation_attempt: Read Post end to end: one recv into a discarded buffer, status line never parsed, return value is the write result. Weighed the header's self-contradiction ('returns as soon as the request is on its way' versus '@return True when the receiver accepted it').
reason: Both SendAsync overloads return whether the whole request was written, not whether the receiver accepted it, so a 400 or a silent close still yields true, contradicting the documented @return. The header text is internally inconsistent, but the specific @return promise is what callers read; low severity.

refutation_attempt: Grepped TARGET for WSAStartup and ws2_32: only Inspector and vendored ENet (lazy). Checked socket_t is SOCKET so a comparison against zero can never hold, that phone links only runtime and core headers, and that the WIN32 test exclusion in UnitTests.cmake is real.
reason: modules/phone never calls WSAStartup, compares the unsigned SOCKET against zero, links no Winsock library, and its socket tests are excluded on WIN32. Start-up failure needs a process where nothing else initialised Winsock and no Windows run was made, so the label should be inferred-strong, not read-verified.

refutation_attempt: Reasoned through thread timing: the worker reads listenSocket_ per accept while Close writes -1 after the atomic listening_ store with no happens-before edge, so ThreadSanitizer would flag it; on accept failure the loop continues without backoff, so EMFILE spins. Distinct from BUG-157.
reason: listenSocket_ is a plain int written by Close while the worker reads it, a formal data race, and a stale or reused descriptor number can reach accept. A persistent accept failure such as EMFILE loops at full speed. Both defects are real but rarely visible; low fits, although the entry bundles two defects.

refutation_attempt: Read the three Read overloads, PageDown and PageUp: each drops the raw IAsyncResult pointer that CompleteReadEXT or CompletePageEXT allocates. Compared Gamer::GetProfile and SignedInGamer::GetAchievements, which delete theirs, and the C adapter's own comment and page routes.
reason: The synchronous wrappers never delete the heap LeaderboardAction that CompleteReadEXT or CompletePageEXT allocate, leaking one small object per call, unlike the two sibling wrappers. CNA's own C adapter records the Read half in a comment. Low severity: one small allocation per read or page turn.

refutation_attempt: Read Initialize's deletion loop, Gamer's setter and GamerCollection's ownership contract: the loop deletes every element of the installed collection, not only gamers Initialize created. The C ABI also exposes both cna_gamer_set_signed_in_gamers_ext and dispatcher_initialize, in separate smoke tests.
reason: Initialize frees every SignedInGamer in the installed collection, including application-owned gamers published through the public setter, contradicting the GamerCollection ownership contract and causing double delete or delete of stack objects if Initialize runs later. No current program combines the two; medium reflects the memory-safety consequence.

refutation_attempt: Compared with decompiled XNA: its GamerJoined add accessor replays allGamers and ProcessGamerJoined inserts then queues, but both run inside one Update, so user code cannot subscribe between. The AddLocalGamer window is CNA-only; the nested-subscription remote case is identical in XNA.
reason: The AddLocalGamer double report is real: the gamer joins AllGamers at once but its event is queued for Update. The AddRemoteGamer nested-subscription variant also occurs in XNA (replay plus queued event within one Update), so it is not a CNA defect and should be dropped from the entry.
read: xna4-decomp Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Net/NetworkSession.cs::GamerJoined add accessor, ProcessGamerJoined, Update, RaiseUpdateEvents, AddLocalGamer

correction.title: NetworkSession::GamerJoined reports a gamer added with AddLocalGamer twice to a handler subscribed between that call and the next Update
correction.summary: AddLocalGamer inserts the new gamer into AllGamers at once and queues its GamerJoin event for the next Update, while subscribing replays GamerJoined for every gamer already in AllGamers, so a handler subscribed in that window is called twice for the new gamer.
correction.expected: Each subscriber sees one GamerJoined per gamer: subscribing replays the gamers already present, later joins are raised once. XNA's AddLocalGamer is asynchronous, so the gamer enters the collections and its event is raised inside one Update call and user code cannot subscribe between the two. CNA's constructor comment states the same intent, avoiding a queued event that would double-fire a replayed join.
correction.actual: AddLocalGamer adds the gamer to LocalGamers and AllGamers immediately and pushes a GamerJoin event that Update raises later. The replay hook installed by the constructor calls each new handler once for every gamer in allGamers_ at subscription time, so a handler subscribed after AddLocalGamer and before the next Update receives the new gamer's join twice. The AddRemoteGamer path (used by the transport inside Update) inserts and queues the same way, but a handler can subscribe in that window only from inside another GamerJoined handler, which XNA's own add accessor and ProcessGamerJoined reproduce, so it is not part of this entry.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp (constructor replay hook, AddLocalGamer, AddRemoteGamer, Update) and the decompiled XNA NetworkSession (GamerJoined add accessor, ProcessGamerJoined, Update, RaiseUpdateEvents, AddLocalGamer); not executed. The replay semantics were read in an unpinned sibling Sharp Runtime checkout.

refutation_attempt: Searched for any IsHost or HostPeer guard in StartHosting, RegisterHost, ReplyToQuery and HandleClientHello: none; UnregisterHost only runs at teardown and EndJoin's constructor calls StartHosting. CNA's own REMED-NET-008 record confirms the HandleClientHello half is unfixed.
reason: A joined SystemLink session registers with LAN discovery and answers queries like a host, and its ENet host handles ClientHello with no host check, so Find lists it and a joiner attaches to the client, splitting the roster from the real host. Medium fits a three-machine LAN game; ENet accept on clients is intended.

refutation_attempt: Compared decompiled XNA ReceiveData(PacketReader) (Resize to the packet size, position 0) with CNA's Write at position 0 on a MemoryStream that only grows, and PacketReader::getLengthProperty. A 20-byte then 8-byte packet leaves Length 20. Weighed merging with BUG-174.
reason: CNA writes each packet at position 0 without setting the stream length, so a reused PacketReader keeps the longer previous Length and stale trailing bytes, where XNA resizes it to the packet. Under CNA's XNA-wins rule this is a bug. Separate from BUG-174: different symptom, different fix.
read: CLAUDE.md::Where FNA and XNA disagree, XNA wins

refutation_attempt: Grepped every writer of maxGamers_ and privateGamerSlots_: only the constructor and public setters; EndJoin passes MaxSupportedGamers and 4, and no transport code sets them from the ServerWelcome. Confirmed decompiled XNA's ProcessUpdateSessionInfo overwrites both from the host.
reason: A joined session reports MaxGamers 31 and PrivateGamerSlots 4 whatever the host chose, because EndJoin passes FNA's placeholders and nothing later updates them, while XNA overwrites both from the host's session info. The client-side full check and its discovery announcements inherit the wrong values.

refutation_attempt: Read the overload, header comment and named test. The header documents the zero return as a preserved FNA quirk, but CNA's CLAUDE.md says XNA wins over FNA, so it stays a bug. The test only calls the overload with an empty queue.
reason: Real bug under CNA's XNA-wins rule: the overload returns 0 instead of the packet size, and the header records that as a deliberate FNA quirk. The entry wrongly says ReceiveDataIntoPacketReaderReturnsZero pins it; that test covers only an empty queue. Not a duplicate of BUG-171.
read: CLAUDE.md::Where FNA and XNA disagree, XNA wins

correction.actual: modules/net/src/Xna/LocalNetworkGamer.cpp declares uint32_t len = 0, never updates it and returns it. modules/net/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Net/LocalNetworkGamer.hpp documents 'Always 0 when a packet was available; 0 when none was, too' as a preserved FNA quirk. LocalNetworkGamerTests.cpp's ReceiveDataIntoPacketReaderReturnsZero exercises only an empty queue (where 0 is also XNA's result), so no test pins the always-zero return for a received packet. Code that loops while (gamer.ReceiveData(reader, sender) > 0) never reads a packet. The reader-resize half of the same overload is CNA-BUG-171.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5 against the decompiled XNA 4.0 LocalNetworkGamer.ReceiveData and CNA's own CLAUDE.md rule that XNA wins where FNA and XNA disagree; not executed. The named test calls the overload with nothing queued, so it never reaches the packet path.

refutation_attempt: Read both send calls and grepped TARGET for SIGPIPE handling. Re-ran the listener's call sequence as a Python loopback model: SIGPIPE 3/3 after an abortive mid-request close, none after a normal close or complete request; the sender's first write after a reset got ECONNRESET.
reason: The listener's reply is sent with flags 0, and a client that aborts mid-request makes recv report the reset, so the reply send raises SIGPIPE and kills a default-disposition process (model reproduced, not CNA code). The sender's single first write did not signal in modelled cases, so that half is only a latent inconsistency.

correction.title: HttpNotificationChannel writes its reply with ::send flags 0, so a peer that aborts its connection mid-request can end the process with SIGPIPE
correction.summary: The listener's 200 or 400 reply is written with no MSG_NOSIGNAL or SO_NOSIGPIPE, unlike CNA's other socket code. After a peer's abortive close has been reported to the worker as a receive error, Linux delivers SIGPIPE on that write, and the default action terminates the game. The push sender omits the flag too, but its single first write did not raise SIGPIPE in the modelled cases.
correction.actual: Listen replies with ::send(connection, response, size, 0) after ReadRequestBody, and Post writes its request with ::send(connection, request, length, 0); neither sets MSG_NOSIGNAL or SO_NOSIGPIPE, and CNA changes the SIGPIPE disposition nowhere. When a client aborts its connection (RST) part-way through a request, the worker's recv reports the reset, ReadRequestBody returns false or a truncated body, and the reply send then fails with EPIPE, so Linux delivers SIGPIPE, whose default action terminates the process. A client that closes normally, or that resets only after sending a complete request, does not trigger it: the write then succeeds or returns ECONNRESET without a signal. The sender's request is its first and only write on a fresh connection, and a reset seen before that write is reported as ECONNRESET without a signal, so the sender half is a latent inconsistency with the Inspector's convention rather than a demonstrated crash path.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading both phone sources at 009d40f5 and searching CNA for any SIGPIPE disposition change (none; only per-call avoidance in the Inspector, X11 and Wayland code). Executed outside CNA: the entry records a g++ probe of the listener's call sequence that was killed by SIGPIPE in 3 of 3 runs, and this review re-ran the sequence as a Python loopback model on Linux 6.12 (SIGPIPE 3 of 3 after an abortive mid-request close, 0 of 3 after a normal close, ECONNRESET without a signal after a complete request followed by a reset, and ECONNRESET without a signal for the sender's first write after the listener reset the connection). The phone module itself was not compiled or run; macOS (SO_NOSIGPIPE) and Windows (no SIGPIPE) were not examined.

refutation_attempt: Recomputed the rounding in Python (639259364967890123 becomes ...176, spacing 128) and checked JsonValue::numberValue is a double and the writer prints integral doubles with %lld. Traced WriteJsonFile: output stream never checked, rename unconditional, fallback write unchecked.
reason: Ticks, ratings and Int64, DateTime and TimeSpan columns pass through double, so present-day values lose low bits, against the header's 'exact round-trip'. WriteJsonFile ignores stream errors and renames the temporary file unconditionally, so a failed write can replace a good store file. Two independent defects in one entry; both real.

refutation_attempt: Read SanitizeStoreFileNameComponent and the load and save paths: the mapping is many-to-one and the file stores no gamertag. Checked the isolation test uses tagA and tagB (distinct after sanitising) and that the four dispatcher stub gamertags stay distinct, so only app-created names collide.
reason: Gamertags that differ only in characters outside letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen (or same-length non-ASCII names) share one achievements file, so their achievements merge, contradicting the per-gamertag isolation the existing test expects. Leaderboards are unaffected because they store raw gamertags. Low: needs free-form local profile names.

refutation_attempt: Compared the 60-entry table (sorted by enum name) with the decompiled XNA enum order and CNA's test comment that the table is indexed directly by ordinal; the string only reaches an empty EXT method. CNA's REMED-NET-004 records the same defect, not started.
reason: presenceModeStrings_ is alphabetical while GamerPresenceMode follows XNA's declaration order, so setPresenceModeProperty picks the wrong string for nearly every mode (SinglePlayer gets 'At Menu'). The value is stored privately and passed to an empty method, so nothing observes it today; a latent defect.

refutation_attempt: Checked NEXTnet.md item 16 for the quoted counts and reverted remedies, that the builder tools and bundled Content/avatar meshes exist, and that no CI test runs the diagnostic or visual-regression script. Nothing re-run; the label 'reproduced' overstates a recorded measurement.
reason: CNA's own NEXTnet.md item 16 records the garment crossings (shirt 64 of 228, pants 21 of 285, shoes 51 of 270) in both poses and the reverted remedies, matching the entry. Nothing was re-run here, so the evidence is recorded-by-cna, not reproduced; no automated test touches the garment meshes.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a documented refusal or exception for Local sessions: none; the header says 'every gamer in the session' and known_gaps claims nothing is missing. Confirmed the drop and both pinning tests, read CLAUDE.md's XNA-wins rule, XNA's SendData docs and SendDataWorker (no session-type branch).
reason: The drop is real and deliberate, but SendData is documented (XNA and CNA's header) as reaching every gamer including the sender, with no session-type carve-out, and known_gaps says nothing is missing for Local. A silent success that discards data contradicts that contract, so it is a low-severity bug, not a gap.
read: CLAUDE.md::Where FNA and XNA disagree, XNA wins

correction.title: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session silently drops every packet, so neither the sender nor another local gamer ever receives it
correction.summary: NetworkSession::Update raises PacketSend events only when real networking is enabled (SystemLink), so SendData in a Local or LocalWithLeaderboards session reports success and delivers nothing, although SendData is documented to reach every gamer in the session, the sender included.
correction.expected: XNA documents LocalNetworkGamer.SendData as sending to all gamers in a session ('This includes the gamer sending the packet') without any session-type qualifier, and describes Local sessions as making it easier to share code between local and online modes; the decompiled SendDataWorker queues every packet regardless of session type. CNA's own LocalNetworkGamer.hpp repeats 'every gamer in the session', misc/known_gaps.md says nothing is missing about Local sessions, and CNA's CLAUDE.md says XNA wins over FNA where they disagree.
correction.actual: LocalNetworkGamer::SendData enqueues a PacketSend event; NetworkSession::Update in modules/net/src/Xna/NetworkSession.cpp delivers it only inside if (ENetBackend::RealNetworkingEnabled(sessionType_)), which is true for SystemLink alone (modules/net/src/Internal/ENetBackend.cpp), so in Local and LocalWithLeaderboards sessions the event is silently dropped, including a packet a local gamer sends to itself or to another local gamer. SendData reports nothing and IsDataAvailable stays false. The drop is deliberate FNA parity, pinned by LocalNetworkGamerTest.SendDataThenReceiveDataRoundtrip and NetworkSessionTypePolicyTest.SendDataStaysFullySyntheticForEverySyntheticType, but no CNA header documents it and misc/known_gaps.md says the opposite.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. The XNA contract is from xna4-spec (LocalNetworkGamer.SendData, NetworkSessionType.Local) and the decompiled LocalNetworkGamer, which has no session-type check; the native XNA kernel that routes packets to local recipients cannot be read, so delivery in XNA's Local sessions is inferred from the documented API. Reclassified from functional-gap because the behaviour is silent, undocumented in CNA's headers and contradicts the SendData contract; the SystemLink branch already contains the local-target delivery a fix would reuse.

refutation_attempt: Counted the Show* overloads (13 XNA plus ShowAchievementsEXT) and read every body: all empty, as is DelayNotifications. Checked docs/xna-4-api-coverage.md records Guide.Show as a documented no-op stub and that the tests only assert no-throw, so no contract is contradicted.
reason: All fourteen Show* overloads and DelayNotifications have empty bodies, recorded in CNA's coverage table as a no-op stub, and tests only assert they do not throw. The LIVE shell has no counterpart here and no local substitute exists, so this is a documented gap, not a violated contract.

refutation_attempt: Read Achievement::GetPicture (throws NotImplementedException), EndGetAchievements (empty name and description), SetPresenceModeStringEXT (empty), the GamerPrivileges and GamerProfile constructors, and grepped for any privilege consumer: none. Every stated fact holds.
reason: Local achievements carry only key, earned flag and time; GetPicture throws NotImplementedException; presence is never published; privileges are a permissive constant that nothing enforces; the profile is synthetic except Region. No catalogue or account exists locally, so this is an intentional gap rather than a contract violation.

refutation_attempt: Read the empty EnableSendVoice and SendPartyInvites, RemoveFromSession (throws NotImplementedException), the never-raised event comments and QualityOfService. All hold, but tests exist: EnableSendVoiceAndSendPartyInvitesAreNoOps, RemoveFromSessionThrows, zero-bandwidth checks and WriteLeaderboardAndTrueSkillEventsAreNeverRaised.
reason: The listed features are unimplemented as described and stay a functional gap, but the entry's 'no test for the missing features' is wrong: tests pin the no-ops, the RemoveFromSession throw, the zero bandwidth fields and the never-raised leaderboard and TrueSkill events.

correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; not executed. The stubs are pinned by tests: LocalNetworkGamerTest.EnableSendVoiceAndSendPartyInvitesAreNoOps, NetworkMachineTest.RemoveFromSessionThrows, the zero bytes-per-second assertions in AvailableNetworkSessionTests.cpp and NetworkSessionTest.WriteLeaderboardAndTrueSkillEventsAreNeverRaised, so an implementation has to change those tests. No test exercises a working version of any of the five features.

refutation_attempt: Read the Emscripten branches of discovery, StartHosting, ConnectToHost and EndJoin: all as described. But the net tests carry Emscripten branches (Find empty, fixed fake-host ports, emscripten_sleep) and CnaTests links -sJSPI=1 for Node, contradicting 'None for any __EMSCRIPTEN__ path'.
reason: The behaviour is as described and stays a platform limitation, but the test statement is wrong: ENetDiscoveryServiceTests assert Find is empty on Emscripten, ENetBackendTests and ENetHostHandleTests adapt SystemLink loopback cases with fixed ports and emscripten_sleep, and CnaTests is linked with -sJSPI=1. Only the process-spawning tests and demos are excluded.

correction.summary: The web build stubs out discovery (Find returns nothing), hosts on a fixed port only a Node.js relay can use, rebuilds a joining session as an outbound-only client and returns from Join before the server welcome; Node.js-run unit tests cover discovery and loopback handshakes, but no browser or two-process test exists.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading at 009d40f5; nothing was built for Emscripten or run in a browser or Node.js during this review. The constraints come from the web platform (no raw UDP, no listening sockets in a tab) and Emscripten's socket emulation, which is why this is a platform limitation rather than a bug; the joined-before-welcome return is the one piece a web-specific wait could change. Emscripten-specific test coverage does exist in source: ENetDiscoveryServiceTests expect Find to be empty on Emscripten, ENetBackendTests and ENetHostHandleTests use fixed ports and emscripten_sleep for the SystemLink loopback and ConnectToHost cases, and cmake/UnitTests.cmake links CnaTests with -sJSPI=1 for Node.js. Only the process-spawning tests (TwoProcessLoopbackTest, the dispatcher hang test) and the networking demos are excluded, so no test joins from a second process and none runs in a browser.
